summary: Off-registry HTTPS tarball dependency fetched and installed on npm install
details: package.json declares a dependency `ltidisafe` whose source is a bare HTTPS tarball URL (https://ltidi.storage.googleapis.com/depenconf/ltidisafe-4.0.3.tgz) rather than a registry version range. On npm install, npm fetches whatever bytes are served at that URL and installs them, running any lifecycle scripts contained in the fetched tarball. There is no version pin, no integrity hash, and no signature check, so the contents are mutable and controlled by whoever controls that storage bucket. The package's own shipped code is an inert stub (index.js is `module.exports = {};`), so the manifest line is effectively the entire delivered payload — the published package functions as a loader for externally hosted code. The implausibly high version (99.9.1) combined with the `sc-hydrate-carousel-price` name is consistent with a dependency-confusion shape intended to win resolution against an internal package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
